analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 0.5% on the week to 7,623.68 as investors digested the start of mega-cap tech earnings, a macro backdrop of oil up and rates down, and a debate over the durability of the AI infrastructure trade.
AI-At-Risk, AI Software and Alternative Asset Managers outperformed on the week, while Goldminers, Copper and IPPs underperformed.

Prime book: US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of last 5, -0.9 SDs 1-year). Single stocks saw the largest de-grossing since late July, and 77% of total net selling was single stocks.

US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile 1-year) while net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 43.4% (0th percentile 5-year). The fundamental long/short ratio fell 0.7% to 1.503 (0th percentile 5-year).

Industrials was among the most net sold sectors. HFs sold the group at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs 1-year) and the US Industrials long/short ratio is 1.67, in the 2nd percentile vs the past year.

Staples and Real Estate were by far the most net bought sectors, the largest net buying since Jul '25 for Staples (+1.8 SDs) and in more than 5 years for Real Estate (+2.4 SDs), pointing to a defensive posture.

The floor has seen about $20bn of net TMT selling over the past 2 weeks across client types and channels, approaching the -$23bn over 2 weeks seen during the July AI selling episode. Little rotation into defensives was seen this week, unlike the prior week.

Managed Money added Brent call positions through mid-October: 32% of the $2.3bn in new gross longs from Oct 6-13 were calls, and about $1bn more was bought through Oct 20. Brent 3-month 25 delta put-call skew cheapened and dealers appear incrementally shorter upside gamma.

Long bond futures completed a round trip from the mid-September selloff. December Ultra-Bond futures are up 6% from the 10/7 low (a 40bp move in implied forward yield) versus about 15bp in 2y yields. Weakness in the AI theme (GS AI basket -16% from 10/7) and HY CDX spreads (+26bp from 10/7) correlated with the rate move.

Elevated rate vols may dampen risk parity demand for bonds, but the negative correlation with risk assets raises diversification value and could draw real money demand. TY put-call skew turned negative this week.

Derivatives: Thursday saw capitulation and de-grossing on AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record, to its lowest since April of last year, and Friday volume was -21% vs 5d avg and -33% vs 100d avg.
Vol of vol is at its highest since April (83rd percentile, 3-year lookback). SPX skew was bid, but desk flows showed less reach for downside protection, attributed to historically low net exposure.
The NDX-SPX implied vol spread blew out to the 98th percentile of 5 years. Thursday's widening was the second largest in 5 years.

EWZ 1-month normalized put-call skew is at all-time highs ahead of the Brazil election. Desk flows were decisively bullish, with interest in EWZ calls and call spreads and in GSBZRATE for a higher-beta play.

Baskets desk view: the market is in a HF deleveraging episode where short term stops matter more than medium term value. The desk says it is time to buy the dip and selectively reposition into AI, starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber. AI vs AI-At-Risk pair (GSPUARTI) is down 13% YTD and S&P ex AI has passed the S&P 500 YTD.
Baskets desk uses GSXUCYCL as a funding short alongside Low Quality expressions, citing slowing growth, higher oil, tighter financial conditions and a tightening cycle.

TMT: NDX was -80bps on the week. Investor conversations focus on what drives price action and what would turn the story, citing the Election, easing macro headwinds or AI data points. There is growing appetite for non-AI idiosyncratic TMT ideas, seen in Consumer stocks.

Financials: a barbell of high quality defensives (P&C insurance, card networks, senior housing REITs) and cheap/value risk-on (regional banks, mid cap payments, lodging REITs, life insurance) outperformed. Blackstone's caution on real estate was followed by an 8% rally in the stock against crowded shorts. Life insurance leaked late in the week on credit spreads.

Industrials -150bps vs the market -30bps, Materials +125bps on geopolitical inflation fears. Movers: BMI +20%, EQPT +19%, ALLE and POOL +15%; AVEX -28%, CRS -25% on a miss and guide-down, FPS -22% on AI/data center weakness and a CFO departure.

Healthcare: ABT cut organic guide, ISRG had light US procedures, DHR cut guide on respiratory. MRNA fell 17.5% and MRK 1.8% after the leaked intismeran data (HR 0.58 vs a <0.6 bar), a sell-the-news reversal.

Next week: S&P implied move through 10/30 is 1.80%. FOMC and BOC Wednesday, ECB Thursday, BOJ Friday. 44% of S&P market cap reports, including MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC Wednesday and AMZN, INTC Thursday, plus ORCL's analyst day. Brazil election results are due Sunday night.

earnings_insights: Healthcare week: ABT lower organic guide, ISRG light US procedures vs elevated expectations, DHR guide cut on respiratory, TMO some initial picking at LSS plus heightened expectations and positioning. Price action was driven more by thematic playbooks than EPS updates.
MRNA fell 17.5% on Thursday after leaked intismeran data with a recurrence-free survival hazard ratio of 0.58 versus a previewed bar of <0.6. This was a sell-the-news reaction.

Industrials earnings: BMI up 20% on mixed earnings with forced short covering, EQPT up 19% after a pre-announced beat and raise, ALLE and POOL up 15% on better than feared earnings, CRS down 25% after a rare miss and guide-down, FPS down 22% on AI/data center weakness and a CFO departure.
Blackstone was the first alt manager to report. It cautioned on real estate and the stock rallied 8%.

Next week, 44% of S&P market cap reports. MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report Wednesday, and AMZN and INTC report Thursday. Semis bellwethers include INTC, SNDK, STX and SEC/Hynix, with focus on ORCL's analyst day. Over 50% of Industrials report. Card networks MA and V report, with V's guide in focus.

NDX-SPX implied vol spread is near 5-year highs (98th percentile). Thursday's widening was the second largest in 5 years.

Brent 3-month normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened while the ratio of 4 delta to 50 delta call implied vol rose. Dealers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

EWZ 1-month normalized put-call skew is at all-time highs ahead of the Brazil election.
US L/S gross leverage 216.1% (64th percentile 1-year, 91st percentile 5-year). Net leverage 43.4% (0th percentile 5-year).
US ETF shorts rose 1.7% (+3.6% month/month), led by shorting in Credit, Large Cap Equity and Asia-Pac ETFs, partly offset by covering in Health Care and Small Cap Equity ETFs.
Macro products (index and ETF) made up 23% of total net selling, with short sales outpacing long buys about 2 to 1.
geopolitical: The US, Iran and Israel are all planning for a return to military engagement.
The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia and Iran disrupted more shipments through the Persian Gulf, which drove Managed Money Brent call buying.
Geopolitical tensions kept inflation fears and global commodity prices elevated, supporting Materials.
The Brazil election results are due Sunday night. Polymarket gives Bolsonaro a 76% chance of winning while local polls show a 0-2.5pt lead for him.
cross_bank_references: GIR's latest piece identified that the Brazil race has tightened since the first round.
